Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): stream ng-analyze RPC notifications through a 64 KiB BufWriter
Issues.Body:
`send_notification` in `ng-analyze/src/main.rs` previously built an intermediate `serde_json::Value` tree via `serde_json::json!` and wrote JSON tokens directly to `StdoutLock`, which wraps stdout in Rust's 1 KiB `LineWriter` buffer. On multi-megabyte `analysisResult` payloads (such as a ~4.1 MB optimized chunk for a target with ~30 UI and CDK `.d.ts` dependencies), this double-serialized every field, allocated ~20 MB of temporary `Value` nodes, and fragmented the stream into thousands of ~1 KiB writes.

Serialize a typed `RpcNotification` wrapper directly through a 64 KiB `BufWriter` around `StdoutLock`, batching writes into larger chunks that bypass `LineWriter`'s 1 KiB buffer while letting the host process drain the pipe concurrently. Streaming through `BufWriter` also avoids multi-megabyte `Vec<u8>` buffer reallocations and overlaps pipe reads with serialization, cutting warm round-trip latency on a 4.1 MB `analysisResult` payload from 130–166 ms to 55–57 ms (vs 66–84 ms for an off-lock `Vec<u8>`) and lowering sidecar peak RSS from 115 MB to 95–97 MB.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): stream ng-analyze RPC notifications through a 64 KiB BufWriter" (#72183)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): fix allowedSources and rootDirs enforcement in OverlayFileSystem
Issues.Body:
When `allowedSources` is configured (for example, in unsandboxed build trees where sibling `.ts` files from other compilation targets live on disk alongside their compiled `.d.ts` files), `OverlayFileSystem` is supposed to hide non-allowed `.ts`/`.js` files so `oxc_resolver` falls through to `.d.ts` dependencies instead of loading undeclared sources.

There were several correctness gaps in how `OverlayFileSystem` enforced that boundary:

- `metadata` and `symlink_metadata` skipped `is_allowed` on `rootDirs` fallback candidates, and `read_link` skipped `is_allowed` entirely, allowing disallowed files under another `rootDir` or through symlinks to remain visible to module resolution.
- Directories whose names end in `.js` (such as `zone.js`) and symlinks pointing to directories were treated as `.js` files and rejected by `is_allowed`, breaking resolution through those directories.
- `resolve_across_root_dirs` and `is_allowed` kept checking shorter `rootDirs` prefixes after matching the longest prefix (diverging from TypeScript's `tryLoadModuleUsingRootDirs` and `ngtsc`'s `LogicalFileSystem`), and `is_allowed` could allow a blocked file if a sibling `rootDir` had a directory or mismatched entry.
- `canonicalize` with `preserve_symlinks` checked `path.exists()` directly instead of resolving relative paths against `self.cwd` through `self.physical.exists`.

This change encapsulates allowlist matching in an immutable `SourceAllowlist` and enforces `is_allowed` consistently across `metadata`, `symlink_metadata`, `read_link`, and `rootDirs` fallbacks:

- `metadata` and `symlink_metadata` now stat the physical path first so directories (including `.js`-named directories and symlinks to directories) are allowed directly without exposing blocked files in sibling `rootDirs`, and pass the `symlink_metadata` result into `is_allowed_with_meta` on cache misses (which also avoids redundant `rootDirs` walks and `canonicalize` calls on missing probes or non-symlink files whose basename cannot match the allowlist).
- `rootDirs` entries are deduplicated while preserving `tsconfig.json` priority for equal-length roots, and prefix matching stops after the longest matching prefix.
- `exists_raw` skips locking `virtual_files` when no virtual files are present, and `canonicalize` with `preserve_symlinks` resolves relative paths against `self.cwd` via `self.physical.exists`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): fix allowedSources and rootDirs enforcement in OverlayFileSystem" (#72182)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): enforce authoritative ModuleFormat and single module-load boundary
Issues.Body:
Host-supplied ModuleFormat values are now authoritative across ng-analyze and the TypeScript
preprocessor layer. Module loads resolve format via LoadResult.format, falling back to
ResolveResult.format, then ModuleFormat::from_path for IdKind::Path modules, and failing with a
HostError when still undetermined. Proactive un-resolved virtual overlays continue to default
to TypeScript unless an explicit FileUpdate.format is supplied.

FileIdInterner records each module's authoritative format so .d.ts classification, TypeScript
source closure filtering, compilation-root gating, and NgModule chunk grouping consult
ModuleFormat rather than path suffixes. AnalysisResult and FileUpdate also carry optional
format metadata so ExpressionPrinter.emitTypes, HMR updates, and declaration-file tracking
honor host-provided formats.

Finally, ResolvedModule::code is removed from internal Rust resolution types while keeping
inline code on the external wire protocol in BatchingHost. AnalysisHost::load is now the sole
module-content path and ResolutionCache never retains module source strings.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): enforce authoritative ModuleFormat and single module-load boundary" (#72181)

Issues.Title: fix(core): route defer block rendering errors through error boundaries
Issues.Body:
### Summary

Previously, `renderDeferBlockState` caught errors thrown while rendering a defer block view (such as component constructor errors) and sent them directly to `handleUncaughtError`, bypassing any enclosing `@boundary` or programmatic `onError` handler.

This PR:
- Rethrows errors in `renderDeferBlockState` when executing synchronously inside `hostLView`'s creation or refresh pass (`getLView() === hostLView`), so synchronous defer errors abort `renderView` / `refreshView` immediately and flow through `@boundary` / `handleViewError` like normal template errors.
- Routes asynchronous defer block rendering errors through `handleViewError` first, falling back to `handleUncaughtError` only if no error boundary handles them.
- Adds unit tests covering `@defer (on immediate)` + `$reset()`, `@defer (when ...)`, creation-mode and update-mode abort behavior, nested `@boundary`, `DeferBlockBehavior.Manual`, `ErrorHandler.onViewError` details, and programmatic `createComponent(..., {onError})`.

Fixes #72165
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): route defer block rendering errors through error boundaries" (#72172)

Issues.Title: NG8021 reports `prefetch when` as matching the main trigger even when the two `when` expressions differ

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): do not report `prefetch when` with a different expression than the main trigger
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The `deferTriggerMisconfiguration` extended diagnostic (NG8021) reports a `prefetch when` trigger as redundant whenever the main trigger is also `when`, even if the two triggers watch different expressions:

```html
@defer (when isOpen(); prefetch when isRequested()) {
  <heavy-cmp />
}
```

```
warning NG8021: Prefetch 'bound' matches the main trigger and provides no benefit. Remove the prefetch modifier.
```

A `when` pair (`TmplAstBoundDeferredTrigger`) has no branch of its own in the check, so it falls through to the generic branch that only compares the trigger classes and never looks at the expressions. The runtime evaluates the prefetch expression on its own, so this prefetch is useful: the dependencies start loading as soon as `isRequested()` is truthy, which can be well before `isOpen()` is.

Issue Number: #72173

## What is the new behavior?

`when` pairs get a branch of their own, next to the reference-based triggers:

- different expressions (`when isOpen(); prefetch when isRequested()`): no diagnostic;
- the same expression (`when ready(); prefetch when ready()`): still reported, since that prefetch really is redundant. The message now names the trigger `'when'`, as it is written in the template, instead of `'bound'` (the name derived from the `BoundDeferredTrigger` class).

**How the expressions are compared.** `BoundDeferredTrigger.value` is the `ASTWithSource` returned by `BindingParser.parseBinding`, so the check compares the trimmed `source` text of the two expressions. The trim is needed because the block parameter keeps the whitespace in front of the `;` (`when ready() ; prefetch when ready()`). I picked the source text because it is the smallest comparison that is easy to trust, and it only errs in the quiet direction: two expressions that are equivalent but written differently (e.g. `a&&b` and `a && b`) are treated as different and produce no warning, so the comparison never adds a false positive. A structural comparison would need either a new AST-equality helper or the `serialize()` function from `expression_parser/serializer.ts`, which is not exported from `@angular/compiler`; I am happy to switch to it if you prefer that.

This follows #67497, which fixed the same false positive for `idle` pairs with different timeouts.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- The same branch is added to the preprocessor's mirror of the check (`packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/src/extended_diagnostics/checks/defer_trigger_misconfiguration.ts`). The spec of the ngtsc check also runs against that mirror through the `test_ngp` target, and with the ngtsc check fixed alone the new cases fail there (the mirror reports `Prefetch 'trigger' matches the main trigger…` for every `when` pair). I know the preprocessor README says external PRs for it are not accepted; if you would rather keep it untouched, I can drop that file and list the new specs in `ngp_known_failures.ts` instead.
- No docs change: the [NG8021 page](https://angular.dev/extended-diagnostics/NG8021) does not describe `when` pairs.
- Tests run locally: `bazelisk test //packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/extended/test/checks/defer_trigger_misconfiguration:all` (`test` and `test_ngp`; the new cases fail without the fix) and `bazelisk test //packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/test:test`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(compiler-cli): do not report `prefetch when` with a different expression than the main trigger" (#72175)

Issues.Title: fix(animations): avoid closure over hostElement in createRenderer
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to a62ae5b04d.

Commit a62ae5b04d extracted `getOrCreateBaseRenderer` out of `AnimationRendererFactory.createRenderer` so that `onRendererDestroy` would not share a V8 closure context with `registerTrigger` (which captured `hostElement`).

However, because `getOrCreateBaseRenderer` is a single-call-site module-private helper, optimizing compilers and minifiers (such as Closure Compiler, Terser, or esbuild) can inline it back into `createRenderer`, putting `onRendererDestroy` and `registerTrigger` back in the same function scope and reintroducing the leak in production builds.

This change extracts `registerTriggers` into a standalone recursive helper so `createRenderer` has no closures capturing `hostElement` at all, making the fix resilient to function inlining (and avoiding a closure allocation per animated component creation).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(animations): avoid closure over hostElement in createRenderer" (#72177)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): replace preprocessor string fingerprints with ChangeKind tracking
Issues.Body:
To decide whether cached template bindings (`FileAnalysis`) and compiled outputs (`ProcessedFile`) remained valid across incremental builds, `HybridCompiler` previously JSON-serialized and hashed each file's `AnalysisResult`, source text, cross-file `<ng-content>` dependency signatures, and emitted `.ng.ts` text (`boundFingerprint`, `processingFingerprint`, and `IncrementalEmitTracker`'s output hash). In `optimize: true` mode, each component's `AnalysisResult` embeds resolved `.d.ts` declaration metadata, so stringifying and hashing those payloads on every build dominated JavaScript incremental overhead even for files whose inputs had not changed.

Replace JSON serialization and string hashing with eager per-file `ChangeKind` invalidation (`Unchanged`, `Dependency`, `ResourceOnly`, `Source`) and reference-keyed `ProcessedFileCache` lookups over `(sourceContent, analysisResult, tcbConfig, remoteScopeKey)`. Files outside the delta closure keep their cached `AnalysisResult` reference in `metadataByFile` without touching their metadata at all. When a pass re-streams a file, `isAnalysisResultEqual` canonicalizes structurally identical `AnalysisResult` objects against `metadataByFile` without string allocation (short-circuiting on file/template scalars and the first differing field) so unchanged files hit `ProcessedFileCache` in constant time once `markChangeKind` deletes invalidated entries.

Direct source edits (including extensionless `idKind: 'virtual'` modules) mark `ChangeKind.Source` and immediately evict cached `FileAnalysis` and `metadataByFile` entries, while external template or stylesheet edits mark `ChangeKind.ResourceOnly` so parsed templates are cleared without discarding cached `.ts` source text. Whenever a re-analyzed file's `AnalysisResult` changes while its own component template inputs remain identical (`areComponentTemplatesUnchanged`), or when a child component's `<ng-content>` signature changes, `markChangeKind` records `ChangeKind.Dependency` so TCBs are re-bound and affected files are re-processed without re-parsing their HTML templates. `IncrementalEmitTracker` compares `ProcessedFile` object references first and falls back to comparing emitted `.ng.ts` strings only when reprocessing produced a new `ProcessedFile`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(compiler-cli): replace preprocessor string fingerprints with ChangeKind tracking" (#72180)

Issues.Title: fix(migrations): avoid leaving blank lines when removing import declarations
Issues.Body:
When `applyImportManagerChanges` deletes an entire `ImportDeclaration`, it previously replaced only `[getStart(), getEnd()]`, leaving the trailing newline (and any leading horizontal whitespace) behind as a blank line.

That blank line splits import blocks and can interfere with editor/formatter import auto-sorting.

This change expands the deletion range in `applyImportManagerChanges` to consume leading horizontal whitespace and a single trailing line break when the removed import declaration is alone on its line (while preserving any trailing comments or same-line code).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(migrations): avoid leaving blank lines when removing import declarations" (#72178)

Issues.Title: fix(core): prevent streaming resource from getting stuck in reloading
Issues.Body:
### Summary

When recomputing `ResourceImpl.state` (a `linkedSignal`), computing `previousStatus` called `projectStatusOfState(previous.value)` without `untracked`. For a resolved resource, `projectStatusOfState` reads `previous.value.stream!()`, registering the previous stream signal as a reactive dependency of `this.state`.

Because `linkedSignal.set()` marks the node clean without clearing producer dependencies from the prior computation, any subsequent emission on that stream signal (e.g., a late emission from a superseded stream or a stream signal reused across reloads) marks `this.state` dirty and recomputes it back to `loading` / `reloading` with the unchanged `extRequest`. Since `extRequest` did not change, `loadEffect` never re-runs, leaving the resource stuck in `reloading` (or `loading`) and causing further `reload()` calls to return `false`.

### Fix

Wrap `projectStatusOfState(previous.value)` in `untracked` so `this.state` only tracks `this.extRequest`.

### Testing

Added unit tests in `packages/core/test/resource/resource_spec.ts` covering:
- Reloading a streaming resource when the previous stream emits after the reload resolves
- Reloading a streaming resource that reuses the same signal across reloads
- Changing `params` on a streaming resource when the previous stream emits after the new load resolves

Verified all 3 tests fail without the fix and pass with it via `bazel test //packages/core/test/resource:resource`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): prevent streaming resource from getting stuck in reloading" (#72179)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): do not treat property names as import name collisions
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The import manager treats any identifier in the file as taken, including object keys and property accesses. With `{Service: '...'}` in a file, the service migration imports `Service as Service_1` even though nothing collides, and then still writes `@Service()`, so the output doesn't compile.

Issue Number: #72168

## What is the new behavior?

Names that can't bind or reference a local symbol (object keys, property accesses, destructuring keys, enum members, import/export names, tuple labels, JSX attributes, statement labels) no longer count as collisions when picking an import name, so the repro gets a plain `import { Service }` and `@Service()`. The names that bind are collected once per file and cached. Generated aliases like `Service_1` still check every identifier, so they match what TypeScript emits. When `Service` really is declared in the file, the import is still aliased and the migration now uses the alias in the decorator.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: forms (signals): number, range and datetime-local bindings throw a TypeError when the model value is Infinity, and the input is left stale
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When the model value of a Signal Forms field that is bound with `[formField]` to `<input type="number">` (also `type="range"` and `type="datetime-local"`) becomes `Infinity` or `-Infinity`, the binding throws a `TypeError` from `HTMLInputElement.valueAsNumber`.

Expected: `Infinity` is handled like `NaN`. The input is cleared and no error is thrown.

Actual: the error is thrown inside the binding. The input keeps its old value while the model holds `Infinity`, and the update of the rest of the component's view is skipped: an interpolation such as `{{ model().average }}` still shows the old value until the next change detection.

Steps:
1. A model `{ total: 10, count: 4, average: 0 }`, `form(model)`, and three `<input type="number" [formField]="...">`.
2. A button that sets `average = total / count`.
3. Click it with count 4: average becomes 2.5 in the model and in the input.
4. Set count to 0 and click again: 10 / 0 is `Infinity`.
5. Result: the error below in the console, the input still shows 2.5, and the text that prints the model still shows 2.5. A second click makes the text show `Infinity` while the input stays at 2.5.

`NaN` (0 / 0) works: the input is cleared with no error. Only `Infinity` and `-Infinity` are missing.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/Dev199092/signal-forms-infinity-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
ERROR TypeError: Failed to set the 'valueAsNumber' property on 'HTMLInputElement': The value provided is infinite.
    at setNativeNumberControlValue
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

Browser: Chrome (also reproduced in a production build)

Package                   Installed Version
@angular/common           22.3.0
@angular/compiler         22.3.0
@angular/core             22.3.0
@angular/forms            22.3.0
@angular/platform-browser 22.3.0
```

### Anything else?

Cause: `setNativeNumberControlValue` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/native.ts` only guards `isNaN(value)` and otherwise does `element.valueAsNumber = value`. Browsers throw for non-finite values. The same code is on `main`.

Suggested fix: treat non-finite numbers like `NaN`:
if (!Number.isFinite(value)) { element.value = ''; } else { element.valueAsNumber = value; }

Workaround: write `Number.isFinite(x) ? x : NaN` into the model.

A realistic trigger is `total / count` with `count = 0`. Not tested: apps that use zone.js, other browsers.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "forms (signals): number, range and datetime-local bindings throw a TypeError when the model value is Infinity, and the input is left stale" (#72157)

Issues.Title: fix(forms): clear native number inputs for infinite signal form values
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When a Signal Forms field bound with `[formField]` to a native number-backed input gets `Infinity` or `-Infinity` as its model value, `setNativeNumberControlValue` writes it to `element.valueAsNumber`. Browsers throw a `TypeError` for infinite values, so the input keeps its old value and the rest of the view update is skipped.

I started from #72157 and checked it against the code.

Fixes #72157

## What is the new behavior?

`setNativeNumberControlValue` already writes `''` for `NaN`. It now does the same for any non-finite value (`!Number.isFinite(value)`), so `Infinity` and `-Infinity` clear the input like `NaN` does and nothing is thrown. The model value is not changed.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

### How I found it

I read `setNativeNumberControlValue` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/native.ts` after seeing #72157. It handles `NaN` but passes every other number straight to `valueAsNumber`.

### Where this can show up in practice

#72157 is a field report: a computed value such as `total / count` becomes `Infinity` when `count` is 0. The same helper is used for `type="range"` and the date/time inputs that take a number model.

### Verification (macOS)

`bazelisk test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test` (Chromium and Firefox).

- New test in `number_input.spec.ts`: sets the model to `Infinity`, then `7`, then `-Infinity`, and checks the input value and the model value each time.
  - Without the fix: Chromium 407 passed, 1 failed (`Failed to set the 'valueAsNumber' property on 'HTMLInputElement': The value provided is infinite.`); Firefox 403 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped (`HTMLInputElement.valueAsNumber setter: Value being assigned is infinite.`).
  - With the fix: Chromium 408 passed, 0 failed; Firefox 404 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped.
- The existing `NaN` tests pass before and after.

Issues.Title: Service worker caches `Cache-Control: no-store` responses for asset group `urls` and serves them to the next user after logout
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

service-worker

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


For URLs matched by an asset group's `urls`, `handleFetch()` answers from CacheStorage whenever it has a copy:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/53ef99a543e037b64c596e9c3e147cb365062cea/packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts#L141-L164

and `fetchAndCacheOnce()` keys in-flight requests by URL only, then stores the response without looking at `Cache-Control`:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/53ef99a543e037b64c596e9c3e147cb365062cea/packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts#L300-L336

So:

- A response sent with `Cache-Control: no-store` is stored and served to later requests for that URL, whatever their credentials. On a shared browser, the next user gets the previous user's response. The [docs](https://angular.dev/ecosystem/service-workers/config) say `urls` resources "are cached according to their HTTP headers", and `no-store` means a cache [must not store the response](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.2.5).
- A request that arrives while another request for the same URL is in flight gets that request's response, even if one was sent with the user's cookie and the other with `credentials: 'omit'`.

Minimal example:

```json
{ "name": "api", "installMode": "lazy", "resources": { "urls": ["/api/**"] } }
```

```ts
await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/login', { user: 'alice' }));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me'));

await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/logout', null));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me', { credentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store' }));

await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/login', { user: 'bob' }));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me'));
```

`/api/me` is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store, private` and `Vary: Cookie`, and returns `{"user":null}` without a session. The last two requests both get alice's response:

```json
{ "user": "alice", "email": "alice@example.test", "request": 1 }
```

Bob's request has no options, so the request's `credentials` and `cache` don't matter here. `Vary: Cookie` doesn't help either: asset groups always match with `ignoreVary: true`, and requests in the worker don't carry the `Cookie` header.

The requests above:

| Request                                                                | Service worker bypassed | Service worker active |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `GET /api/me` as alice                                                 | alice, request 1        | alice, request 1      |
| `GET /api/me` after logout, `credentials: 'omit'`, `cache: 'no-store'` | `null`, request 2       | alice, request 1      |
| `GET /api/me` as bob                                                   | bob, request 3          | alice, request 1      |

Then, as alice, a URL that isn't cached yet, and 50 ms later the same URL with `credentials: 'omit'`:

| Request                                     | Service worker bypassed | Service worker active |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `GET /api/me?race=…`                        | alice, request 4        | alice, request 2      |
| `GET /api/me?race=…`, `credentials: 'omit'` | `null`, request 5       | alice, request 2      |

Both cases use the setup of GHSA-95qp-cmmw-mgqv (precondition 2), but neither is the request rebuilding fixed in #68904. That request now keeps `credentials: 'omit'` and `cache`, and the server never gets a cookie for those requests: in both cases the worker answers without sending them. The advisory also notes that CacheStorage is governed by `ngsw-config.json` and `ngsw-bypass`, not `Request.cache`. The first case is about the response's own `Cache-Control`, which the docs say `urls` follow, and the second one doesn't come from CacheStorage.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

See https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/ng-service-worker-cache-bypass

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.16.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.13.0
Operating System  : win32 x64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/service-worker   │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else?

I think we can consider this a bypass of https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-95qp-cmmw-mgqv

Issues.Title: router: `withErrorBoundaries` docs say event handler errors are caught, but an error thrown in a `(click)` handler does not render the route's `errorComponent`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The JSDoc of `withErrorBoundaries()` says:

> errors thrown within routed components (lifecycle hooks, template bindings, resource loaders, and event handlers) are caught by the RouterOutlet

In my app, an error thrown from a `(click)` handler of a routed component is not caught: the route's `errorComponent` is not rendered, `onError` is not called, the component stays on screen, and the error only goes to the global `ErrorHandler` (browser console).

Errors thrown in the constructor are handled as documented (the `errorComponent` is rendered).

```ts
{ path: 'ctor',  component: CtorPage,  errorComponent: ErrorFallback },  // constructor throws -> fallback rendered
{ path: 'click', component: ClickPage, errorComponent: ErrorFallback },  // (click) handler throws -> fallback NOT rendered
```

Expected: either the `errorComponent` is rendered for the click handler error, or the documentation does not list event handlers. I cannot tell which of the two you intend, so I am reporting the mismatch.

Also not caught in my tests: an error in a child component's `output()` handler, and in a host `(click)` listener. Same result in a production build.

From reading the code, listener errors seem to go through `executeListenerWithErrorHandling` in `@angular/core`, which calls `handleUncaughtError`, and not through the boundary lookup used for other errors. That is only my reading of the source; I did not debug it further.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/Dev199092/error-boundary-event-handler-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
ERROR Error: save failed
    at ClickPage.go (...)

(only in the browser console; the page does not change)
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

Package                   Installed Version
@angular/build            22.3.0
@angular/cli              22.3.0
@angular/common           22.3.0
@angular/compiler         22.3.0
@angular/compiler-cli     22.3.0
@angular/core             22.3.0
@angular/forms            22.3.0
@angular/platform-browser 22.3.0
@angular/router           22.3.0
typescript                6.0.3
```

### Anything else?

Workaround that I verified: catch the error in the handler, store it in a signal, and rethrow it from a template binding. Then the boundary renders the `errorComponent`.

Not tested: zone.js apps, other browsers, SSR.

Issues.Title: compiler: `ngNonBindable` on the root element of an `@empty` block crashes the template compiler ("All attributes should have an element-like target", no file or line)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? No ### Description An element with `ngNonBindable` that is the root element of an `@empty` block makes the template compiler fail with an internal error. The message names no file, line, component or template, so in a larger project it is very hard to find the cause. ```html @for (item of items; track item) {

{{ item }}

} @empty {

No items {{ not interpolated }}

} ``` Expected: the template compiles, and the paragraph shows the curly braces as plain text. Actual: `ng build` fails with `Angular compilation emit failed` and `Error: All attributes should have an element-like target.` With `ng serve` already running, the page keeps its old content and the browser shows an error overlay ("Angular compilation initialization failed"). If the first build fails, `ng serve` does not start at all. It only fails when the element is the (single) root element of the `@empty` block. Any tag fails (`div`, `span`, `p`, `input`, `svg`). It works: - when the element is wrapped in ``, `` or another element inside `@empty`; - when `@empty` has two root elements; - when `ngNonBindable` is on a child element; - in `@if`, `@else`, `@switch` and `@defer` blocks and in the `@for` body. I found it with a template fuzzer (3 of 200 random templates crashed) and minimised one of them. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/Dev199092/empty-nonbindable-repro ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ✘ [ERROR] Angular compilation emit failed. [plugin angular-compiler] Error: All attributes should have an element-like target. at lookupElement$2 (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:9027:11) at Object.specializeBindings [as fn] (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:9050:28) at transform (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:19316:13) at compileComponentFromMetadata (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:22653:3) at ComponentDecoratorHandler.compileFull (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/bundles/chunk-IRDAAWGT.js:13386:17) ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.3.0 Angular : 22.3.0 Node.js : 24.20.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 Package Installed Version @angular/build 22.3.0 @angular/cli 22.3.0 @angular/common 22.3.0 @angular/compiler 22.3.0 @angular/compiler-cli 22.3.0 @angular/core 22.3.0 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else? Workaround: wrap the element in `` (one line), or put `ngNonBindable` on a child element, or use `@if (items.length === 0)` instead of `@empty`. I did not test older Angular versions, and I do not know the cause. It looks like the attribute handling for the root element of an `@empty` block, but that is only a guess.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "compiler: `ngNonBindable` on the root element of an `@empty` block crashes the template compiler ("All attributes should have an element-like target", no file or line)" (#72161)

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #72157

When a `[formField]` bound to a number-like input (number, range, datetime-local, or date-type inputs with a numeric model) gets `Infinity` or `-Infinity` from the model, `setNativeNumberControlValue` writes it to `valueAsNumber`, which throws. The input keeps its old value and the rest of the view update is skipped.

## What is the new behavior?

Issues.Title: feat(devtools): improve hydration mismatch debugging experience
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## Summary

Improves the hydration mismatch debugging workflow in Angular DevTools without modifying existing console error message strings:

### 1. Core hydration debug metadata (`fix(core)`)
- Stores an optional, dev-mode-only `WeakRef<Node>` to the live mismatched DOM node (or the expected parent element with `isParentFallback: true` when the node is missing) and runtime `errorCode` (`NG0500` / `NG0501` / `NG0502`) on `__ngDebugHydrationInfo__`.
- Fixes embedded-view mismatch attribution (`@if`, `@for`, `@defer`) by using `lView[DECLARATION_COMPONENT_VIEW][HOST]` in `validateMatchingNode` and `validateNodeExists` instead of `lView[HOST]!` (which is `null` in embedded views).
- Passes the raw `describeDomFromNode(node)` snippet in `validateSiblingNodeExists` (`NG0501`) instead of duplicating the `Actual DOM is:` header.
- Zero production bundle impact (verified against `//packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:symbol_test`).

### 2. DevTools backend & extension overlays (`fix(devtools)`)
- Prevents `hydration-overlays.ts` from throwing `Unsupported hydration status highlighting: dehydrated` when dehydrated components (`ngh`) are present (e.g. `@defer` incremental hydration or siblings left unhydrated after an earlier mismatch).
- Includes root components (`<app-root>`) when collecting mismatch overlays.
- Highlights the exact mismatched child DOM element via `actualNode?.deref()` (falling back to `parentElement` for `Text`/`Comment` nodes, and to the component host element on older Angular versions).
- Adds optional serializable `errorCode`, `hasActualNode`, and `isParentFallback` fields to `HydrationStatus` in the protocol (never passes DOM `Node` instances over `postMessage`).
- Adds backend/extension actions to inspect the exact mismatched node in the **Elements** panel (`inspect(inspectedApplication.findHydrationMismatchNodeByPosition(...))`), highlight it on hover, or log the live DOM node to the **Console**.

### 3. DevTools UI (`feat(devtools)`)
- Moves hydration mismatch details out of the fixed-height (`[itemSize]="18"`) virtual-scroll `ng-tree-node` row (where leaf components had no expand chevron and `<pre>` blocks broke row heights) into a dedicated `<ng-hydration-error-view>` inside the property pane.
  - Highlights the `<-- AT THIS LOCATION` line inside `Expected DOM` / `Actual DOM` snippets.
  - Shows an error code pill with a direct link to the error reference doc (`angular.dev/errors/NG05xx`).
  - Exposes **Inspect DOM node** (or **Inspect parent** / **Inspect host** fallback for older Angular versions) and **Log node** action buttons, highlighting the live node on hover.
- Adds a compact mismatch banner at the top of the **Components** tree to auto-expand ancestors and jump straight to the failing component(s) (with prev/next controls when multiple mismatches exist).
- Adds a toolbar toggle icon for **Show hydration overlays** when hydration is detected.
- Clarifies copy on `dehydrated` components when a mismatch exists elsewhere in the tree.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

All new fields on `__ngDebugHydrationInfo__` and `HydrationStatus` are optional, so Angular DevTools remains backward-compatible with older Angular versions.

Refs #56392
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(devtools): improve hydration mismatch debugging experience" (#72156)

Issues.Title: refactor(core): disambiguate repeated node paths in hydration errors
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type - [ ] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? When hydration encounters a mismatch in a template with repeated nodes, `@for` iterations, or identical branches, the error message only displays the immediate parent element and the mismatched node: - Identical sibling branches (both labelled with attributes further up the tree and unlabelled branches) are indistinguishable. - Repeated direct children (`
  • ...
    • ...
` or `@for`) show no sibling index (`child element 3 of 4`) and hide `nextSibling` behind `…`. - `class` and `style` attributes are omitted from expected `TNode` snippets (`stringifyTNodeAttrs` stops at the first `AttributeMarker`), and `stripNewlines` strips *all* spaces (`card primary` -> `cardprimary`). - `validateNodeExists` (`NG0502`), `validateSiblingNodeExists` (`NG0501`), `nodeNotFoundError`, and `nodeNotFoundAtPathError` omit the declaring component name, `Actual DOM` (on missing nodes), and `ClassDebugInfo` (`filePath:lineNumber`). - `markRNodeAsHavingHydrationMismatch` used `lView[HOST]`, which is `null` inside embedded views (`@if`/`@for`/`@defer`), dropping DevTools mismatch metadata. Related to #56392 (alternative to PR 70249; does **not** add DOM validation or empirical HTML-nesting checks). ## What is the new behavior? Improves dev-mode hydration error messages (`NG0500`, `NG0501`, `NG0502`) to pinpoint **exact** mismatch locations across repeated elements and branches without repeating large vertical ancestry trees inside both `Expected` and `Actual` snippets: - **Single compact CSS-style `DOM path:` line** (omitted for trivial single-child root mismatches; shows `Expected`/`Actual DOM path:` only when the parent diverges): - Walks across component boundaries so enclosing ancestors remain visible (e.g. `app > section.panel > user-row:nth-of-type(2) > div.name`). - Uses `#id` (safely quoting non-identifier IDs such as `[id="1"]` / `[id="-1"]`), identifying attributes (`data-testid`, `aria-label`, `name`, `role`, `type`), and up to 2 valid CSS class tokens. - Disambiguates duplicate sibling elements sharing the same base selector with `:nth-of-type(N)` (e.g. `li.row:nth-of-type(3)` inside `@for`, or `section:nth-of-type(2)` for unlabelled branches). - Appends a 1-based sibling position (`(child element 3 of 4)` / `(child node 2 of 3)`) when the mismatched node sits inside a parent with multiple siblings. - Compacts deeply nested paths (`> 8` segments) by preserving notable landmarks (`#id`, identifying attributes, component hosts, and `:nth-of-type(N)` branches) instead of blindly slicing the tail. - Keeps DevTools `expectedNodeDetails` / `actualNodeDetails` compact (`
` displays stay clean without duplicating `DOM path:`).
- **Symmetric surrounding sibling snippets**: `describeDomFromNode` shows both `previousSibling` and `nextSibling`, and both expected/actual snippets omit spurious leading/trailing `…` when no extra siblings exist.
- **Missing-node `Actual DOM is:`**: Shows the actual parent element contents when `node === null` (`NG0500` and `NG0502`).
- **Template `class`/`style` and preserved whitespace**: Includes static `classesWithoutHost`/`stylesWithoutHost` in expected DOM snippets and collapses whitespace runs to single spaces in `shorten()`.
- **Consistent component identity & DevTools attachment**: Surfaces declaring component name + `filePath:lineNumber` (`ClassDebugInfo`) across `NG0500`, `NG0501`, and `NG0502`, and attaches mismatch info via `lView[DECLARATION_COMPONENT_VIEW][HOST]` so embedded views work properly in DevTools.

### Examples

Repeated `@for` row (`Carol`'s `` replaced by ``):
```text
NG0500: During hydration Angular expected  but found .

DOM path: app > ul.users > li.row:nth-of-type(3) > div.name

Angular expected this DOM:



  …  <-- AT THIS LOCATION
  …



Actual DOM is:



  …  <-- AT THIS LOCATION


```

Repeated direct siblings (`
  • ` #3 of 4 replaced by ``):
```text
NG0500: During hydration Angular expected 
  •  but found .

DOM path: app > ul (child element 3 of 4)

Angular expected this DOM:


      
  …
  
    • …
      • 
  
    • …
      •   <-- AT THIS LOCATION
  …

    

Actual DOM is:


      
  …
  
    • …
      • 
  …  <-- AT THIS LOCATION
  
    • …
      • 

    
```

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

All changes are dev-mode-only and tree-shaken from production bundles. Tested with:
- `bazel test //packages/platform-server/test:test`
- `bazel test //packages/platform-server/test:event_replay_test`
- `bazel test //packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:symbol_test //packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:test`

Issues.Title: feat(forms): add `derive()` schema rule for signal forms
Issues.Body:
## Description

Draft prototype proposing a declarative `derive()` schema rule in `@angular/forms/signals` to address #65467 (updating a form field's value from other fields or external signals without user-written `effect()` blocks).

### Proposed API

Two progressive overloads matching existing rules (`validate`, `min`, `disabled`, `validateAsync`) and Angular's `linkedSignal` mental model:

```ts
form(model, (p) => {
  // 1. Shorthand (reactive computation; `linkedSignal(fn)` semantics)
  derive(p.total, ({valueOf}) => valueOf(p.quantity) * valueOf(p.unitPrice));

  // 2. Shorthand + config
  derive(p.slug, ({valueOf}) => slugify(valueOf(p.title)), {
    when: ({state}) => !state.dirty(),
  });

  // 3. Source-driven options (`source` tracked, `compute` runs untracked)
  derive(p.state, {
    source: p.country, // accepts SchemaPath, LogicFn, or Signal
    on: 'change', // preserves initial/hydrated value; narrows `ctx.previous` as defined
    fieldState: 'reset', // clears dirty/touched/parseErrors when updated
    compute: (country, {previous}) =>
      statesByCountry[country]?.includes(previous.value) ? previous.value : '',
  });
});
```

#### Config options
- **`when`**: Reactive guard (`LogicFn<TValue, boolean, TPathKind>`). Inactive rules do not evaluate `source`/`compute`.
- **`on`**: `'always'` (default, runs on activation and on changes) or `'change'` (captures active snapshot as baseline on initial activation and on `when` re-activation, only writes on subsequent changes while active; TypeScript narrows `ctx.previous` to non-nullable `{source, value}`).
- **`equal`**: Custom `ValueEqualityFn<TValue>` for comparing target values (defaults to `Object.is`).
- **`sourceEqual`**: Custom `ValueEqualityFn<TSource>` for comparing successive `source` values (defaults to `Object.is`).
- **`fieldState`**: Interaction state behavior on write — `'preserve'` (default), `'reset'` (clears `dirty`, `touched`, parse errors and cascades to descendants), or `'dirty'`.

### Key Behavioral & Architectural Details
- **Per-field `effect()` via `createManagedMetadataKey`**: Mirrors `validateAsync`'s lifecycle (`node.structure.injector`), so each derivation only re-runs when its own tracked inputs change (O(1) in `applyEach` arrays), cleans up automatically when fields become orphaned, and composes naturally with `schema()`, `apply()`, `applyEach()`, `applyWhen()`, `applyWhenValue()`, and recursive schemas.
  - *Why not a single root polling `effect()` + hybrid sync flush?* A root polling loop re-evaluates every derivation in the form on any change, an eager sync flush during `form()` construction throws `NG0950` when reading `input.required()`, and hybrid flushing creates split sync-vs-async timing between `field.value.set()` and `model.set()` / external signals.
  - *Why not user-written `effect()` outside `form()`?* It does not compose with `schema()`, `applyEach()`, or `applyWhen()`, lacks per-item cleanup, and pushes `untracked()` / `on: 'change'` / `reset()` re-baselining boilerplate onto every caller.
- **Multiple rules per field**: Coexist in declaration order (`trim` → `toLowerCase` → `slice` pipeline, or multiple triggers driving the same field).
- **Availability states**: Unlike validators, `derive()` continues to run when a field is `readonly`, `disabled`, or `hidden` (enabling `readonly(p.total)` + `derive(p.total, ...)` and clearing hidden fields).
- **`reset(value)`**: Re-baselines `on: 'change'` rules inside the reset subtree so loading a new snapshot (e.g. `form().reset({country: 'CA', state: 'ON'})`) does not wipe `'ON'`, while `on: 'always'` rules still settle.
- **Array element identity**: Copies the parent's tracking `identitySymbol` when replacing an array item object so `FieldNode` identity (`dirty`, `touched`, bindings) is preserved.
- **Cycle detection**: Per-rule microtask write guard throws `NG01922` (`RuntimeErrorCode.DERIVATION_CYCLE`) on non-converging cycles.

### Open Discussion Points
1. Naming: `derive` vs `derived` vs `compute` / `link`, and `compute` vs `computation` (mirroring `linkedSignal`).
2. Whether `compute` in the `{source, compute}` form should run **untracked** (implemented here to prevent accidental self-triggers) or **tracked** (matching `linkedSignal`).
3. Whether `source` should accept bare `SchemaPath` shorthand (`source: p.country`) vs strictly `LogicFn` (`({valueOf}) => valueOf(p.country)`).
4. `fieldState: 'reset'` when the newly derived value happens to equal the existing value (`equal(current, next) === true`).

### Verification
- `//packages/forms/signals/test/node:test` (55 specs in `derive.spec.ts` + compile-time assertions in `types.spec.ts`; 639/639 passing)
- `//packages/forms:forms_api` & `//packages/forms:forms_errors` (updated `goldens/public-api/forms/signals/index.api.md`)
- `//packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_lib` build verified
- `//packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals:symbol_test` (0 new symbols — `derive()` is tree-shaken when unused)

Refs #65467

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): guard aborted requests across rendering and serialization
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When a request is aborted during SSR rendering:
- `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` can still perform asset reads, run `html:transform:pre` hooks, invoke `renderAngular()`, or run Beasties `inlineCriticalCss()` after `request.signal` has already aborted.
- `renderAngular()` does not check `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed` (post-`whenStable`), or `destroyPromise` consistently across bootstrap, stability, and `content()`, only clears `renderTimeoutId` on the first `destroy()` call, detaches abort listeners two microtasks after `content()` settles, and can leave `asyncDestroyPlatform()` unresolved if `platformRef.destroy()` throws.

Companion framework fix: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139
Related issue: #34754

## What is the new behavior?

- Short-circuit `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` on `request.signal.aborted` before asset reads, `html:transform:pre` hooks, `renderAngular()`, redirect response creation, and critical CSS inlining, and uniformly await `result.destroy()` when aborting inside the response `ReadableStream`.
- Keep immediate platform destruction on abort in `renderAngular()` (relying on the framework teardown fixes in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139 instead of deferring destruction or adding fallback timeouts).
- Guard `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed`, and `destroyPromise` consistently across `renderAngular()` and `content()`, clear `renderTimeoutId` on every `destroy()` call, detach abort listeners before settling `content()`, and wrap `platformRef.destroy()` in `try`/`finally` inside `asyncDestroyPlatform()`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

Issues.Title: augmentChunkHash hashes only input source maps, so an output-map change keeps a lazy chunk name while its debugId (and bytes) change
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The same gap exists since #34583, but it shows up on a toolchain update: 22.2.6 → 22.3.0.

### Description

#34583 made the chunk optimizer's `augmentChunkHash` include the hashes of the *input* source maps of a chunk's modules, so that a change that only affects the source map renames the chunk (#34574). The `//# debugId=` comment injected after naming is derived from the *output* source map, though, and the output map can change while every input map stays the same.

Updating `@angular/build` from 22.2.6 to 22.3.0 does exactly that for vendor-only lazy chunks. In our production build, two lazy chunks that hold only third-party code (SheetJS and jsPDF, loaded with `import()`) kept their file names, and their JavaScript was byte-for-byte identical apart from the trailing comment:

```
-//# debugId=e8aee844-1ba7-543c-be31-811b9fc51bb2
+//# debugId=fb140939-ab0f-576a-a399-540d2ee6737b
```

In the chunks' `.map` files, `sources` and `sourcesContent` are identical; only `names` and `mappings` differ (the newer minifier maps the same output differently). The input maps are unchanged, so `augmentChunkHash` returns the same value, Rolldown's code hash is the same, and the file name is the same while the bytes differ.

With `subresourceIntegrity` on, a browser or CDN that holds the old copy under that name fails the integrity check against the new `index.html`, and the lazy import fails. The same applies to any update that changes only how the output is mapped (minifier, Rolldown, or the debug ID computation), so every toolchain bump can reintroduce it.

Related: #34674 reports the same symptom for `main` and `polyfills`, and proposes naming files from their final bytes after debug IDs are injected. That approach would also cover this case; hashing the output map (or the final file contents) in `augmentChunkHash` would cover it for optimized lazy chunks.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. An application with source maps on for scripts, `subresourceIntegrity: true`, and enough lazy chunks for the chunk optimizer to run (3 or more), including at least one lazy chunk that holds only a third-party library loaded with `import('<package>')`.
2. Build with `@angular/build` 22.2.6 and keep `dist/`.
3. Update `@angular/build` and `@angular/cli` to 22.3.0 without changing application code, and build again.
4. Compare the two `dist/` folders: list files that exist in both with the same name and different contents. The vendor-only lazy chunk is among them, and `diff` shows only the `//# debugId=` line changed.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource '<origin>/chunk-XXXXXXXX.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
@angular/build    : 22.3.0 (previous build: 22.2.6)
@angular/core     : 22.3.0
TypeScript        : 6.0.3
Node.js           : 24.22.1
Package manager   : npm 11.19
OS                : macOS and Linux (CI)

Build options: `sourceMap: true`, `subresourceIntegrity: true`, `outputHashing: all`, production configuration.

Build options: sourceMap: true, subresourceIntegrity: true, outputHashing: all, production configuration.
```

### Anything else relevant?

(The error above is the shape of the browser error when a stale cached copy is served; our CI caught the name collision before deploy, so we did not ship it.)

Workaround we used: change what the app imports from each library (a local module that re-exports only the used members), which changes the rendered chunk code and so its name. `namedChunks: true` only changes the readable prefix; the `[hash]` part is computed the same way, so it does not prevent this.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "augmentChunkHash hashes only input source maps, so an output-map change keeps a lazy chunk name while its debugId (and bytes) change" (#34774)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): validate path options against MCP roots in host execution
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

In the MCP server (`ng mcp`), `createRootRestrictedHost` only checked `effectiveCwd` before calling `executeNgCommand` / `startNgProcess`. Option flags forwarded from `run_target` via `serializeOptions` (such as `--output-path`, `--out-file`, `--output-file`, `--ts-config`, `--runner-config`, `--karma-config`, etc.) were passed directly to the spawned `ng` command without verifying that their paths remained within the allowed MCP roots.

For example, invoking `run_target` with `{"target": "build", "options": {"output-path": "/path/outside/root"}}` allowed the spawned builder to escape the root-restricted boundary, recursively clean the target directory via `deleteOutputDir` (since `deleteOutputDir` only rejects exact equality with the workspace root), and write build outputs outside allowed MCP roots.

Issue Number: b/587904432

## What is the new behavior?

- **`createRootRestrictedHost` (`packages/angular/cli/src/commands/mcp/host.ts`)**:
  - Validates path-bearing, glob-based, and output-directory CLI flags passed to `executeNgCommand` and `startNgProcess` against the active allowed MCP roots (supporting both `--flag=value` and separate `--flag value` forms, camelCase/kebab-case/snake_case keys, dot-notation, negation forms with `=`, `--runner-args`, and passthrough args after `--`).
  - Rejects output directory flags (`--output-path`, `--output-dir`, etc.) when the resolved target is outside allowed roots **or** is equal to / an ancestor of the effective workspace directory or any allowed root.
  - Validates compound relative output flags (`--out-file`, `--resources-output-path`) against both `cwd` and any supplied output directory, regardless of argument order.
  - Leaves non-filesystem flags intact (e.g., `--base-href`, `--deploy-url`, `--serve-path`, `--route`, `--routes`, `--filter`, `--delete-output-path`, `--output-hashing`, `--output-mode`, and boolean values for union options such as `index`, `server`, `serviceWorker`, and `runnerConfig`).
  - Hardens real-path resolution in `createRootRestrictedHost` to follow dangling symlinks, handle intermediate symlinks before `..` segments, and check exact path separator boundaries (`..` directory prefixes such as `..hidden.txt` inside a root are allowed).
- **`serializeOptions` (`packages/angular/cli/src/commands/mcp/tools/run-target/options-serializer.ts`)**:
  - Tightens option key validation to require a leading alphanumeric character (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$`).
  - Rejects null bytes (`\0`) in string option values.
  - Normalizes `excludeKeys` comparison so case/separator variants cannot bypass excluded keys (e.g., `watch`).
- **`run_target` strategies (`build-target-strategy.ts`, `generic-target-strategy.ts`, `unit-test-strategy.ts`)**:
  - Re-throws non-`CommandError` exceptions (such as root access-denied errors from `createRootRestrictedHost`) instead of catching them as failed command execution logs.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

`deleteOutputDir` in `@angular/build` was intentionally left unchanged so direct `ng build` CLI invocations with explicit external absolute output paths (e.g. `/tmp/...`) continue to work as expected; confinement is enforced at the MCP host boundary.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): validate path options against MCP roots in host execution" (#34773)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): resolve installed @angular/core version in list_projects MCP tool
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The `list_projects` MCP tool works out `frameworkVersion` by walking up from the workspace directory to the first `package.json` that declares `@angular/core`, then passing the declared value to `semver.minVersion`. If the declared value isn't a semver range, `semver.minVersion` throws. That happens with pnpm/yarn catalogs (`catalog:`, `catalog:angular`), `workspace:*` and `npm:` aliases. The tool then reports a versioning error for the workspace (e.g. `Invalid comparator: catalog:`) and leaves `frameworkVersion` unset.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

The version now comes from the installed `@angular/core/package.json`, resolved with `createRequire` the same way the `get_best_practices` tool does it. How the dependency is declared no longer matters.

- Resolution starts from the workspace's `angular.json` file rather than its directory. `createRequire` searches from the parent directory of the path it's given, so starting from the directory would skip the `node_modules` of nested workspaces such as `apps/web`.
- If `@angular/core` isn't installed or its version can't be read, `frameworkVersion` is left unset and no error is reported.
- The upward `package.json` search and its cache are removed.
- The output schema is unchanged.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@ngtools/webpack): elide const enum imports when rewriting an import declaration
Issues.Body:
## How I found it

I started from #34760 and checked it against the code. In `elide_imports.ts`, once a declaration has to be rewritten because a value specifier is unused (here a class used only as a constructor parameter type), the remaining specifiers are no longer left to TypeScript's own elision. `isValueAlias` treated the const enum as a runtime value, and because its property access counts as a use, the specifier was kept in the rewritten import. With default options the const enum is inlined and the module has no such export, so webpack reports `export 'Period' (imported as 'Period') was not found`.

## Where this can show up in practice

- An `@ngtools/webpack` / `@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` build where a component or service imports a const enum together with a class that is only used as a type (for example a DI constructor parameter), as in the repro in #34760.
- Shared constants modules that export a `const enum` next to injectable services are a common layout, so more projects on the webpack builder may hit this. This is my estimate; the issue's repro is the only report I know of.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When an import declaration is rewritten, a const enum specifier whose references are inlined is still kept, so the emitted import names an export that does not exist at runtime and the webpack build fails.

Issue Number: Closes #34760

## What is the new behavior?

`isValueAlias` now treats an alias that resolves to a const enum as a non-value alias, unless `preserveConstEnums`, `isolatedModules` or `verbatimModuleSyntax` keeps const enum references (the same options TypeScript itself checks). The specifier is then dropped like a type-only one.

New test in `elide_imports_spec.ts` (`emitDecoratorMetadata` is false): a declaration that imports a const enum and a type-only class, where the class specifier is removed. The expected output has no import and the inlined value `1 /* MixedEnum.A */`.

## Testing

- I could not run the bazel target on the machine I used (macOS). Instead I ran `elide_imports_spec.ts` with jasmine and TypeScript 6.0.3 together with copies of `elide_imports.ts` and `spec_helpers.ts`:
  - without the fix, the new test fails (the output still contains `import { MixedEnum } from './mixed'`) and the other 38 pass;
  - with the fix, all 39 pass.
- As a reference I compared plain `tsc` emit for the same source with the transformer output:
  - with default options both drop the import;
  - with `isolatedModules` both keep it and the reference is not inlined;
  - with `preserveConstEnums` alone `tsc` drops the import and the transformer keeps it. The enum object is emitted in that mode, so the import resolves.
- End to end, I used the repro project from #34760 (Angular 22.2.6, `@ngtools/webpack` 22.2.7). `ng build` fails with the error above. After applying the same change to the installed `elide_imports.js`, the build succeeds and the bundle contains `"month" /* Period.Month */`.
- `prettier --check` passes on both files. CI here is the real check for the bazel target.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: ng add @angular/ssr fails with TypeError when an NgModule in the app module file has no bootstrap array
Issues.Body:
### Command

add

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

I think before the server schematic started inferring the app component name (commit ea1143dd, April 2025). I have not run an older release to confirm.

### Description

`ng add @angular/ssr` (and `ng generate server`) crashes on an NgModule-based app when one of the `@NgModule` decorators in the file that `main.ts` bootstraps has no `bootstrap` array. The cases I hit:

1. The root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` instead of `bootstrap: [...]` (Angular Elements apps, AngularJS hybrid apps that bootstrap through `UpgradeModule`).
2. The file declares another `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` (for example a small shared module) before the root module.

In `packages/schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, `resolveNgModuleBasedData` loops over the module's `@NgModule` decorators and does:

```ts
const bootstrapProp = getMetadataField(node, 'bootstrap').find(...);
const componentIdentifier = (bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression)
  .elements[0] as ts.Identifier | undefined;
```

When `bootstrapProp` is `undefined`, the optional chain stops at `initializer` and `.elements` is read from `undefined`. The function is meant to return `null` in that case: the caller in `server/index.ts` already falls back to `App` / `AppModule` when nothing is found. So the schematic stops with a TypeError instead of using the fallback (case 1) or the right module (case 2).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new demo --no-standalone`
2. In `src/app/app-module.ts`, remove `bootstrap: [App]` and add `ngDoBootstrap() {}` to `AppModule`.
3. `ng add @angular/ssr`

Or, for case 2, keep `bootstrap: [App]` and put this above `AppModule` in the same file:

```ts
@NgModule({ exports: [] })
export class SharedModule {}
```

I reproduced this with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (workspace -> `application --standalone=false` -> edit the module -> `server` and `ssr` schematics). Both schematics throw for case 1, and `server` throws for case 2. The unmodified app works.

### Exception or Error

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')
    at resolveNgModuleBasedData (node_modules/@schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.js:65:14)
```

### Your Environment

```text
@schematics/angular 22.3.0
@angular-devkit/schematics 22.3.0
Node.js 22.23.5
```

### Anything else relevant?

Skipping decorators that have no `bootstrap` field (`continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above it) is enough to fix both cases: case 2 then finds `AppModule`, and case 1 falls through to the existing fallback. I have a patch with two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` and can open a PR.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): skip NgModules without bootstrap when resolving the app component
Issues.Body:
## How I found it

A lint pass (oxlint `no-unsafe-optional-chaining`) flagged the server schematic's module lookup in `utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, and I read the code to check it. The optional chain in `(bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression).elements[0]` stops at `initializer`, so `.elements` is read from `undefined` whenever `find` returns nothing. I then reproduced it with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (details in #34761).

## Where this can show up in practice

- An Angular Elements app, or an AngularJS hybrid app, whose root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` and has no `bootstrap` array: `ng add @angular/ssr` stops with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')`.
- A module file that declares a small shared or routing `@NgModule` above the root module: the first decorator has no `bootstrap`, so the lookup throws before it reaches `AppModule`.
- A root module with `bootstrap: []` left over from a refactor.

This is my estimate; I have not seen a field report.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`resolveNgModuleBasedData` throws when an `@NgModule` decorator in the bootstrapped module's file has no usable `bootstrap` array, so the `server` and `ssr` schematics fail instead of using the next module or the existing `App` / `AppModule` fallback in `server/index.ts`.

Issue Number: Closes #34761

## What is the new behavior?

Decorators without a `bootstrap` array are skipped with `continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above. If no module has one, the function returns `null` and the caller's fallback applies.

Two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` (non standalone application):

- a shared `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` declared before the root module: the root module's component is still used;
- a root module that uses `ngDoBootstrap()`: the schematic completes and writes `app.module.server.ts`.

## Testing

- I could not run `bazel test //packages/schematics/angular:test` on the machine I used (linux-arm64; `rules_browsers` has no chromium for that platform, so analysis fails).
- Instead I transpiled the changed `server/index_spec.ts` and `app_component.ts` with the repo's TypeScript and ran the spec with jasmine against the published `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0:
  - without the fix, the two new tests fail with the TypeError above and the other 21 pass;
  - with the fix, all 23 pass. The unchanged `ssr/index_spec.ts` (10 specs) also passes with the fix.
- `prettier --check` passes on both files.
- CI here is the real check for the bazel target.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): destroy the platform of an aborted request once it…
Issues.Body:
… is stable

Aborting a request destroyed the platform while an app initializer or an `HttpClient` request was still pending, which could end the server process. The platform is now destroyed once the application is stable, or after 10 seconds.

Fixes #34754

Issues.Body:
